title.narrative: NIHR Policy Research: NIHR Global Health Research portfolio Value for Money framework and assessment

description.narrative:
A UK and low- and middle-income country (LMIC) research partnership that is developing a Value for Money (VfM) framework to assess the NIHR Global Health Research (GHR) portfolio. The work is being undertaken by Ecorys in partnership with Access Health – India and an international Public Health consultant. Commencing in October 2025, this six-month award is based in the UK with expected fieldwork in select LMICs where NIHR-funded research is delivered. The primary objectives are to provide evidence of the value created through global health research, improve accountability for Official Development Assistance (ODA) spending, and strengthen future decision-making.
Key activities include: • Development and refinement of a framework via stakeholder consultations, document review and benchmarking. • Development of a draft VfM framework inclusive of indicators, feasibility assessment, and refinement of programme‑level and portfolio‑level assessment tools. • VfM framework testing through case studies (via further interviews and fieldwork), applying it across programmes and the selected awards. • Gathering and synthesising of evidence, before producing recommendations to support long-term assessment and learning across the GHR portfolio.

The award has 5 objectives: 1. Develop a clear and practical Value for Money (VfM) framework. To design a VfM framework for the NIHR Global Health Research (GHR) portfolio that explains how value is created across programmes and awards, including economy, efficiency, effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, equity, and sustainability, using evidence from interviews, document review and benchmarking. This will support DHSC and NIHR to assess the value of investments in global health research.
2. Define indicators and a set of instructions that can be used consistently. To identify and describe indicators for assessing value across the GHR Portfolio and produce a set of instructions that explain different levels of progress. This includes specifying the data needed for each indicator and ensuring that indicators can be used with available programme and award evidence.
3. Test and refine the framework through case studies. To apply the draft VfM framework to case studies drawing on selected programmes and awards, test indicator feasibility, refine the instructions, and identify strengths and challenges in the assessment process.
4. Gather evidence across the portfolio to assess value. To collect evidence from programme and award documents, interviews, focus groups, and site visits to understand how value is created through NIHR‑funded research, including effects on research capacity, partnerships, community engagement, policy influence and health systems.
5. Produce VfM assessments with confidence ratings. To synthesise available evidence and apply the VfM set of instructions to generate assessments of progress for each programme, including a confidence rating for each indicator and clear explanations of evidence quality, gaps and assumptions.
